gen-nixie-one-gf-koho: Generously opened curves make the text here read cleanly and without fuss. KoHo handles the steady reading, while Nixie One brings the retro-tech display look with no brush-style swell anywhere.
gen-nixie-one-gf-kumbh-sans: Nixie One keeps its line constant and its curves open. Nixie One does the nostalgic display work, while Kumbh Sans, with terminals cut well short of the bowl, handles the everyday reading.
gen-nixie-one-gf-lato: Nostalgic and a little retro-tech, Nixie One draws open curves with a single line weight, and Lato sits beneath it. Lato's wide, barely curled s curves give the display lines a straightforward partner.
gen-nixie-one-gf-lunasima: Lunasima sets clean, contemporary text whose c tips never creep toward touching, beneath a Nixie One display heading. The heading's untapered strokes and the body's open tips make a tidy match.
gen-nixie-one-gf-m-plus-1: Retro-tech in open curves: Nixie One holds a constant line and looks fondly backward. But M PLUS 1, with big open eyes on every e and a, gives that nostalgia a modern, flat-lined footing.
gen-nixie-one-gf-m-plus-2: M PLUS 2 is approachable and professional, with a gaping c opening and a fixed nib width that keep text easygoing. Nixie One adds the nostalgic, retro-tech display note above.
gen-nixie-one-gf-m-plus-rounded-1c: Nixie One never swells or thins within a stroke, keeping its open curves quietly retro-tech. M PLUS Rounded 1c, with terminals that stop short of curling back in, carries the text with approachable ease.
gen-nixie-one-gf-mandali: Nixie One brings a nostalgic display look, its open curves and untapered strokes free of any quill-like pressure. The standout quality is Mandali's clean, generous entry into the e.
gen-nixie-one-gf-manjari: Nixie One holds a constant line through every open curve, giving headings a nostalgic, retro-tech feel. But Manjari, with wide unclosed terminals and a steady line weight, should read smoothly and approachably across paragraphs.
gen-nixie-one-gf-metrophobic: Nixie One has a pencil-line consistency and open, gappy curves. Its nostalgic look pays off in big, brief headings, while Metrophobic follows a smooth, unobstructed path around each bend in the text.
